Care robot for homes and assisted-living/rehab facilities, in production since its CES 2026 debut.

sdk: Open-source SDK with low-level access; NVIDIA Isaac Gym training support

Mass production underway with an order book over 800M CNY; swaps its own battery in 3 minutes.

sdk: Closed platform; Agility Arc cloud orchestration + enterprise APIs

sdk: SDK with ROS compatibility; developer platform actively maintained
price_note: Estimated between $125,000 and $150,000+ — not officially published, enterprise sales only, no North American channel. Full-size 175 cm research and service platform with 12-DoF hands.

sdk: Closed — Helix VLA stack, no public SDK; internal and partner deployments only
price_note: No public price. The widely quoted $20,000 is a stated consumer target, not an offer: there is no pre-order or retail channel, and all units go to internal programs and partner deployments (BMW Spartanburg). Enterprise pricing is negotiated.

sdk: Closed, internal Tesla use only; no SDK or developer access
price_note: Tesla has never published a price for Optimus and has no order, reservation, waitlist or lease channel: as of 2026 tesla.com carries no Optimus product page. The widely quoted $20,000-$30,000 is a long-term target at volume stated by Tesla's CEO, not a price. Any site taking Optimus pre-orders or deposits is not affiliated with Tesla.

sdk: Closed; partner deployments only (Hyundai, Google DeepMind), no public SDK
price_note: Not publicly sold, no MSRP — analyst estimates run ~$130k–320k. The production electric Atlas debuted at CES 2026 and the entire 2026 output is contracted (Hyundai Metaplant, Google DeepMind); Hyundai targets 30,000 units/year by 2028.

sdk: unitree_sdk2 (C++/Python), ROS 2 support
price_note: Official retail by version: Air $1,600, Pro $2,800, Go2 X $4,500; EDU Standard $11,190, EDU Plus $13,205, top EDU configurations up to $19,430. Unitree cut prices across the line in 2026 ahead of its IPO.

price_note: Launched at 12,999 CNY (~$1,800) in Xiaomi's Chinese retail, still sold there with no successor; international resellers charge ~$3,000.

price_note: Dealer range by configuration: from $2,890 minimum listing / Basic RC $5,400, Venture $9,500, Pro $12,999, LiDAR version $18,900. Research platform.

price_note: Dealer guide prices: ~$65,000 for the X30, ~$74,800 for the X30 Pro; some dealers quote on request only. Industrial IP67 quadruped for autonomous inspection.

sdk: unitree_sdk2 (C++/Python), ROS 2 support

sdk: Spot SDK (Python), gRPC API

sdk: TCP/IP SDK (Python, C++, ROS), DobotStudio Pro

sdk: JAKA App graphical programming, TCP/IP SDK, ROS adapter

sdk: KRL (KUKA Robot Language), ROS-Industrial support

A full cell with gripper and integration runs ~$60k.

Estun publishes no list price for this model.

sdk: Closed platform; enterprise integrations (NVIDIA GR00T partner), no public SDK

sdk: Closed; proprietary Turing AI chips (2,250 TOPS), no public SDK

European distributor listings run higher, around EUR 735-905 depending on variant. A desktop-class educational cobot rather than an industrial workhorse: 250 g payload, 280 mm working radius.

sdk: ABB RobotStudio, Wizard Easy Programming, RAPID

sdk: Smart Pendant / hand-guided teaching, MotoPlus SDK, ROS driver

This is an estimate, not an offer. IP67-rated and hand-guided teachable, aimed at damp or splash-prone industrial environments.

sdk: ANYmal API and workforce/inspection software suite; enterprise integration, no consumer SDK
price_note: ANYbotics does not publish a retail price; ANYmal is sold as a configured enterprise deployment (robot, docking, software, onboarding, support). Treat all figures as estimates, not offers.

All figures come from procurement disclosures and documented estimates, not a public price list.

Figures are distributor offers, not a manufacturer list price.

All hardware and software IP was released under open-source licenses on the way out.

Cost figure refers to the published BOM, not a sale price.

Commercial deliveries began in China in late 2025 with international rollout during 2026; treat the range as an estimate pending a formal offer.

Higher trims (EDU and above) with onboard NVIDIA Orin compute cost more; final configuration pricing comes via quotation, and current reseller terms require a full deposit before order confirmation. One of the few full-size humanoids with a published entry price.

sdk: Developer platform for research and education with secondary-development support; optional 11-DOF dexterous hands, 3D LiDAR and voice interaction
price_note: MagicLab operates a contact-sales model and has not published official pricing for the Z1. Distributor listings quote the compact research/education model from about $52,800. Enterprise configurations are quoted separately.

sdk: Developer SDK with commercial and education editions; end-to-end neural motion control (RL + imitation learning), 360-degree LiDAR and depth cameras
price_note: EngineAI executives indicated a target price of RMB 150,000-200,000 (about $20,500-27,400) when global sales opened in late 2024. Distributor listings for export configurations quote substantially higher, up to roughly $54,000. The spread reflects commercial vs education editions and regional markups.

In mid-2026 Sanctuary shifted its commercial focus toward licensing its "Physical AI" software for other companies' industrial robot hardware, while Phoenix's hydraulic hands remain in development. Press reports place comparable research-grade humanoids in the six-figure range, but no official figure exists for Phoenix.

sdk: Neuraverse fleet-learning OS and app ecosystem; NVIDIA Thor compute with Isaac GR00T integration, modular exchangeable forearms and hands

Distributor pricing tiers have shifted through 2026 as enterprise configurations were reorganized.

sdk: Deep Robotics SDK, ROS support
price_note: The X20 has been superseded by the X30 (roughly $65,000-75,000 at US distributor listings) and is labeled discontinued on the US site, though it remains on the global catalog. Treat this as an estimate - the manufacturer sells by quotation only.

sdk: Deep Robotics SDK, ROS support
price_note: US distributor listings price the wheel-legged Lynx M20S at $59,995 and the M20 Pro (dual 96-line LiDAR, autonomous charging) at about $61,200 - a figure also confirmed directly on Deep Robotics' own US shop. sdk: Deep Robotics SDK, ROS support

sdk: MiR Fleet software, REST API
price_note: MiR sells mostly through request-a-quote distributor engagements, but at least one US distributor now lists a fixed, purchasable price of $64,790 for the base MiR250 unit. sdk: LocusOne fleet platform
price_note: Locus does not sell Origin units outright - it is deployed under a Robots-as-a-Service model with hardware, software, integration and support bundled into the subscription. Press reports place typical RaaS rates at roughly $2,000-4,000 per robot per month on 12-36 month terms. Equivalent hardware value is estimated by press at $25,000-50,000 per unit.

sdk: Geek+ Robot Management System (RMS)
price_note: Geek+ sells its goods-to-person P-series project-based, so no official list price exists for the flagship P1200R. Distributor listings for P-series units run from about $35,000 for the mid-range P800R up to the mid-$60,000s, with the 1,200 kg P1200R at the upper end - treat the range as an estimate. Full system cost also includes fleet software and workstations.

sdk: AGILOX X-Swarm intelligence
price_note: AGILOX publishes no list price for the ONE, and neither do its distributors, all of which are quote-only. AGILOX does publish the structure of its rental offer - a fixed base fee plus a variable fee per operating hour over 12-60 months, alongside short-term rent and leasing through partners - but discloses no rate for any of them. No published price, rental rate or procurement figure for the ONE exists.

sdk: PUDU Cloud / Open API
price_note: US resellers list the industrial T300 at $20,990 for outright purchase, with the lifting variant priced separately. Pudu and its partners also offer the robot under Robot-as-a-Service subscription terms. This is one of the few industrial-payload AMRs with a public sticker price.

sdk: Closed (German Bionic IO)

Passive textile exosuit with a mechanical on/off clutch that cuts back muscle strain by 20-40%.

Xiao Di debuted as a working prototype in early August 2026 at BYD's Di Space showroom in Zhengzhou, where the company plans to place two to three units per dealership as a greeter that explains vehicles to customers. BYD has not said whether the robot will ever be sold to third parties.

sdk: AimMaster control client; Linksoul platform for enterprise task customization. No open public SDK terms published.

Mass-production unit costs of roughly $150,000-$170,000 have appeared in press reports, but those are reported cost estimates, not a purchasable price. As of 2026 the GR-1 is no longer in Fourier's lineup, which has moved on to the GR-2 and GR-3.

Per-unit figures around $130,000 in press reports are estimates of pilot cost, not a quoted price. Figure 02 has since been superseded by Figure 03.

sdk: Open developer stack: public source repository (kuavo_opensource), SDK, documentation, simulation platform and 20+ demo cases; open embodied-AI manipulation datasets.

ROBOTERA has not published a price for STAR1 and offers no purchase channel; the robot was presented as a high-speed locomotion demonstrator, best known for its Gobi Desert running record. Per-unit figures near $50,000 and $120,000 appear in secondary reports, but they conflict and none traces to a manufacturer announcement, so both are treated as estimates.

sdk: rby1-sdk - official Python and C++ SDK, Apache 2.0, on GitHub
price_note: Rainbow Robotics announced pre-order pricing itself: $80,000 for the research platform and $120,000 for the commercial platform, VAT excluded, with deliveries from October 2024. The price excludes the optional high-performance 3D recognition sensor and the Master ARM teaching kit; ordering runs through the manufacturer's sales team. This is a wheeled bimanual mobile manipulator rather than a biped.

sdk: Neuraverse OS with NVIDIA Isaac GR00T foundation models; C++ SDK, digital twin and teleoperation in the Pro tier
price_note: NEURA lists the Mini on its own reservation store at EUR 19,999 (Standard) and EUR 29,999 (Pro), about $23,100 to $34,650. A refundable EUR 100 reservation fee is credited against the purchase; the Pro premium buys 12-DoF dexterous hands, the C++ SDK, digital-twin access and teleoperation. Shipping was announced for April 2026; taxes, shipping and support contracts are excluded.

No price and no sales channel. Mobileye completed its $900 million acquisition of Mentee Robotics on February 3, 2026, and expects first on-site customer proof-of-concept deployments in 2026, with series production targeted for 2028. Older press figures around $35,000, and a roughly $20,000 future unit cost, are unconfirmed projections rather than offers.

Clone Robotics publishes no price. Its own pre-order page invites reservations for a limited run of 279 units but states no unit price, no deposit and no delivery date. Figures circulating in press and forums run from about $20,000 to over $200,000 and none traces to the manufacturer. No complete Alpha has been publicly demonstrated walking unsupported.

AI2 Robotics publishes no list price and sells through enterprise contracts in China. A September 2025 bulk order was reported at close to RMB 500 million for over 1,000 robots, which implies roughly RMB 500,000 (about $69,000) per unit - but that is an average across three years of deployment at multiple sites, not a purchasable price. A separate press report quoting 'from about $15,000' is unverified and irreconcilable with the order value, so no figure is published here.

US distributor listings quote $25,000 to buy the Whiz commercial vacuum outright, or robot-as-a-service starting around $699/month, with an alternate comparison-table figure of about $1,042/month depending on term length. SoftBank Robotics itself publishes no price and sells by quote; the subscription bundles hardware, installation, training, software updates and support, while filters, dust bags, brushes and replacement batteries are extra.

sdk: ROS (Ubuntu LTS, RT Preempt), MoveIt!, ros_control
price_note: PAL Robotics sells TIAGo by quote only, with no published list price. The only manufacturer-linked figures date from the 2015 launch (roughly EUR 30,000 base without arm, EUR 50,000 with a 7-DoF arm, EUR 60,000 with the five-fingered hand); those predate the current hardware by a decade and are not treated as a current price. Configuration - arm count, laser range, end-effector, AI kit, software packages - drives most of the cost.

sdk: Python SDK, ROS 2 Humble, LeRobot (open source)
price_note: Reachy 2 launched at a publicly stated $70,000, quoted by Hugging Face's CEO and widely covered in the tech press after Hugging Face acquired Pollen Robotics in April 2025. Reduced configurations (stationary, single-arm) were quoted lower before launch. The price covers the robot platform; shipping, duties, spare parts and training are not included.

sdk: ROS 2 and Python SDK (open source), Stretch AI
price_note: Hello Robot publishes an open list price of $24,950 for Stretch 3 on its own product site, in the standard configuration with dexterous wrist, gripper camera and second head camera. The maker has since introduced Stretch 4 at a published $29,950, so Stretch 3 is now the previous generation. Price excludes shipping, duties and optional end-effectors.

Boston Dynamics has never published a price for Stretch; it has been sold by quote since commercial availability in 2022. Figures of $300,000-$500,000 circulating online are third-party estimates rather than offers. Announced fleet deals (a $15M DHL Supply Chain pre-order, a $10M NFI order) cover many robots plus deployment and service and cannot be divided into a unit price.

sdk: NeuraPy API, NR easy drag-and-drop GUI; EtherCAT/IO-Link, Ethernet/IP, PROFINET, Modbus TCP/RTU
price_note: European distributor listings put the LARA 5 at EUR 18,900 excl. VAT (about $21,800), with the wider family running EUR 16,500 for LARA 3 to EUR 26,900 for LARA 15. The price covers robot, control box and teach panel; gripper, tooling, integration and VAT are extra. NEURA itself quotes on request.

sdk: Python NeuraPy API, NR easy GUI, optional low-level controller/sensor access; GPIO, Modbus TCP/RTU
price_note: European distributor listings show MAiRA S at EUR 37,500 excl. VAT (about $43,300) and MAiRA M at EUR 39,500 (about $45,600); NEURA does not publish MAiRA pricing itself and sells on quotation. The figure excludes VAT, gripper, optional force-torque sensor, integration and support.

sdk: Full ROS integration (EtherCAT stack), Python/C++ API, Gazebo model; source and schematics under NDA
price_note: Shadow Robot published EUR 110,000 for the full 20-DoF Shadow Hand Plus, including shipping, installation, training and support (about $127,000); the same manufacturer post prices a cut-down 2-finger 7-DoF hand at about EUR 45,000. The figure comes from Shadow's own pricing article and has not been restated since, so treat it as an anchor rather than a live quote - the company sells on request.

sdk: Unitree secondary development (high- and low-level), ROS 2, NVIDIA Isaac Sim support
price_note: Unitree lists no price for the A2 on its own site (contact sales); US reseller listings show A2 Standard at $31,900 and A2 Pro at $40,900, both currently out of stock. Prices cover the robot with dual batteries and exclude shipping, duties, the wheeled A2-W variant and expansion compute docks, which are quoted separately.

Wandercraft publishes no list price. Atalante X is a medical device sold to rehabilitation institutions under contract, and in France through central public purchasing agencies with multi-year instalment options. Press reports around the US launch put European hospital units at roughly $176,000 each (about EUR 150,000) - a reported figure rather than a quoted price.

sdk: AgiBot Botnet software support; motion development and swarm control tools
price_note: Listed at $44,560 on AgiBot's own global online store, quoted directly in USD. The price covers the robot, battery pack, battery and accessory chargers, wireless e-stop, wireless controller and transport cart, with a 1-year / 3,000-hour warranty. Shipping is quoted separately at roughly $500-$3,000 depending on destination, and customs duties and taxes are the buyer's responsibility.

Listed at $24,240 on AgiBot's own global online store, quoted directly in USD, covering the robot, battery, charger, remote controller and microphone. Shipping is quoted separately at roughly $500-$3,000 depending on destination, and customs duties and taxes are the buyer's responsibility. Sits between the open-source X1 developer kit and the full-size A2 series in AgiBot's lineup.

AgiBot publishes no price for the X2 Ultra: its own store lists the robot as contact-sales only, supplied through enterprise agreements. It adds 3D LiDAR, an RGB-D camera and 5 more degrees of freedom over the base X2, which does carry a public $24,240 price.

sdk: Python and C++ SDK with open hardware interface (Education Edition only)
price_note: LimX Dynamics' own store lists TRON 1 Standard Edition at $15,000 and the Education Edition at $25,000, both purchasable directly. The Standard package includes the robot body, three interchangeable foot modules, battery, charging dock, handheld controller, haulage rope and roll cage; the SDK and secondary-development toolchain come only with the $25,000 Education Edition.

sdk: Python and C++; ROS 1 / ROS 2; Isaac Sim, MuJoCo and Gazebo simulation support
price_note: At its December 2025 launch, LimX Dynamics priced the base stationary dual-arm TRON 2 configuration at 49,800 CNY (about $7,000), open for pre-order on the manufacturer's own site and independently confirmed by multiple outlets covering the launch. EDU configurations add $20,000 for the dual-arm EDU kit and $25,000 for the full 3-in-1 EDU kit (dual-arm, bipedal and wheeled-leg modules). US resellers list the 3-in-1 EDU kit substantially higher, around $33,000, with freight and customs quoted separately.

sdk: Secondary development supported; upgradeable firmware, Gigabit Ethernet expansion
price_note: Booster Robotics announced the K1 Geek Edition at $5,999 at its October 2025 launch, quoted in USD by the maker, with a $4,999 promotional price during the launch window only. The Geek price covers the 22-DoF robot with 48 TOPS compute, a 2Ah battery, carrying case and a 3-month warranty. The Education (117 TOPS) and Professional (200 TOPS) editions add a 5Ah battery and a 1-year warranty but carry no publicly listed price.

sdk: Secondary development supported, with an embedded reinforcement-learning locomotion stack
price_note: Listed at $7,680 on AgiBot's own global online store, alongside the D1 Pro at $3,200 and D1 Edu at $6,080, quoted directly in USD. Shipping, customs duties and optional payload modules (LiDAR, depth camera, RTK, 4G/5G, video transmission) are not included.

Unitree's own store checkout prices the As2 Air at $3,100 and the As2 Pro at $4,650; the As2 EDU carries Unitree's $100,000 contact-sales placeholder rather than a real price and is excluded from this range. Prices exclude shipping, duties and optional sensor payloads, and the Air variant is currently backordered.

sdk: C++/Python SDK over Ethernet with position and force control; Ubuntu host, ROS support
price_note: Listed at $15,999 on Unitree's own store and marked ready to ship, with a further $1,000 per unit shipping charge stated on the product page. The higher-payload Z1 Pro variant is backordered and not separately priced there. End effectors beyond the standard gripper, duties and taxes are not included.

sdk: Open-source ROS 2 and Python SDK; 3D SLAM navigation and data-collection tooling
price_note: Published at $29,950 on Hello Robot's own purchase page, up from $24,950 for Stretch 3. The price includes the compliant gripper, battery and ballast, wall power supply, Aruco tag kit, gamepad and pistol teleop controllers, tools and cables, with a 30-day return window and a 1-year warranty. Add-ons are priced separately.

Preorders open on JD.com (official channel) with a 3,000 CNY deposit: 119,800 CNY (~$16,500) for the semi-torso U1 Lite, 169,800 CNY (~$24,000) for the mid-tier U1 Pro, and up to 880,000/990,000 CNY (~$121,000/$136,500) for the flagship full-body U1 Ultra (female/male). Over 13,000 units reserved as of the June 30, 2026 launch event; first deliveries due no later than September 15, 2026, so nobody has one in hand yet.

Authorized US resellers publish an outright purchase price of $13,995-$14,000, covering the robot, first-year software and a one-year warranty; freight, on-site mapping and staff training are quoted separately. The same resellers now offer it on subscription from $479/month.

US distributor listings run from $6,500 for a base configuration to a $12,999 quoted MSRP, with $10,000 the most common published figure; the price covers the robot, standard trays and first-year software, but not freight, installation or site mapping. A subscription alternative is published from $270/month. The spread reflects configuration and dealer rather than a manufacturer list price - Pudu publishes none.

US distributor listings publish $15,000-$17,999 for outright purchase, the higher figure quoted as MSRP before freight and installation. Lease-to-own runs roughly $1,000-$1,250/month over 12-24 months. The price covers the four-tray robot, pager and charging dock; a spare hot-swap battery and elevator integration are extra.

Sold only on subscription - no outright purchase price is published. Relay Robotics' CEO has stated the subscription works out to about $75,000 over three years (roughly $2,080/month) with all maintenance and support included; earlier press reports put the lease near $2,000/month. Cost varies with the number of floors, elevator integrations and fleet size, so every deployment is quoted.

An authorized US reseller publishes $22,500 for outright purchase or $1,195/month on subscription, covering the robot, elevator-integration software and first-year support but not the building-side elevator controller work, which is quoted per property. Bear Robotics has since retired the model: its product page returns 404 and the Servi Lift is absent from the company's sitemap, so what remains is reseller stock.

LG publishes no MSRP; an authorized US reseller lists $17,900 for outright purchase or $746/month on subscription, covering the robot, software and first-year support but not freight, mapping or elevator integration. LG's own US business site currently returns no in-production ServeBot listings and marks the drawer-type LDLIM21 as discontinued, so availability should be confirmed before ordering.

Yunji's Hong Kong IPO prospectus discloses an actual 2024 average selling price of RMB 13,100 for the RUN delivery robot - about $1,820 - and Chinese retail listings have appeared around RMB 21,800 (~$3,030). The lower figure is a disclosed average realised price to hotel customers rather than a list price a buyer can take, so the range spans both. Both prices fell sharply from RMB 23,200 in 2022.

Sold only as robot-as-a-service at $5,400 per month with no upfront cost; the fee covers hardware, software, warranty, preventive maintenance and 24/7 bilingual support, while POS integration and extended analytics are paid add-ons. No outright purchase price has ever been published. For reference, the previous-generation Flippy 2 was offered at $3,500 per month plus an $11,000 installation fee.

Hyphen's CEO stated on the record in December 2025 that the automated makelines cost between $50,000 and $100,000 to buy, the spread depending on configuration, and that customers often reach payback in under a year. Leases and pilot deals are offered as an alternative to outright purchase. The stated range covers the unit itself and does not spell out kitchen retrofit, integration or ongoing service.

US distributor listings price the bare robot at $23,800, with the auto-charging dock a separate $1,000 accessory and the bundle with the enhanced workstation listed from $29,500. Subscription is offered from $989 per month on a 36-month term. Prices exclude sales tax, freight, installation, training and wear parts.

A US reseller lists the C30 at $12,200 including the 110V charging station and free domestic shipping; a European distributor lists the same machine at EUR 11,880 excluding VAT. Rental is offered from about $349 per month on a two-month minimum. Prices exclude VAT and duties, installation, training and consumables.

Not for sale: Unitree unveiled this locomotion prototype on August 18, 2026, saying it was built in just over three months. The company disclosed a top running speed and a standing jump height but no price, no hands or end-effectors, no production timeline and no order channel — it says the machine remains a work in progress.

sdk: Nori Lab (laptop app), Skills Marketplace
price_note: Manufacturer's own site lists the Nori A3 at $1,688 full price with no deposit, for a second, limited production batch shipping fall 2026. It is a consumer device controlled and trained through a laptop app rather than a turnkey enterprise deployment.

sdk: Open-source SDK, simulator and RL training stack on GitHub (Apache-2.0)
price_note: Pollen Robotics (owned by Hugging Face) opened preorders on 2026-08-27 at an introductory $399 before tax and shipping, the same price across all four colorways. First deliveries are targeted before Christmas 2026 for North America and Europe; this is a small, open-source educational biped, not a labor platform.

ZEALS Corporation (Tokyo) opened sales and deployment consultations for the D1 on 2026-08-05, pricing it from ¥5,000,000 per unit (about $31,300 at current rates), per the company's own launch announcement. ZEALS is targeting 100 units of production within fiscal 2026, starting with hospital and eldercare pilots — this is a first-generation robot with no delivered-unit track record yet.

AgiBot has not published an official price for the Expedition A3, a martial-arts/exhibition humanoid unveiled at a Shanghai gala in February 2026. Conflicting analyst estimates of $45,000–$110,000 circulate on aggregator sites but do not trace to a manufacturer announcement or distributor listing, so no figure is shown here.

EngineAI's own official page lists China domestic entry pricing at 180,000 CNY (about $25,000), rising to $80,800 for the top international Max edition. The T800 is sold only in China as of August 2026, amid a broader US import restriction on Chinese humanoid and quadruped robots.

The world's first Ex-certified (Zone 1 ATEX/IECEx explosion-proof) legged robot, built for oil & gas, chemical and mining inspection in hazardous zones. Sold only as a custom enterprise deployment; ANYbotics publishes no price.

Industrial semi-humanoid with dual-arm force control and autonomous battery swapping, launched June 1, 2026 for manufacturing and warehouse environments running the maker's own embodied foundation model. Sold via direct enterprise deployment; no public price disclosed.

Legless, wheeled general-purpose humanoid launched June 22, 2026 for logistics, hospitality and food-service tasks, with dual 7-DoF arms and a 4-DoF torso reaching up to 1.9 m; deployed only via Robot-as-a-Service contracts with 8–12 week onboarding, no public unit price.

Heavy-duty wheeled dual-arm robot launched January 2026 for factory material handling, with an industry-leading 50 kg continuous dual-arm payload; in active deployment at CATL battery-manufacturing sites. Enterprise sales only, no public price.

sdk: Lightberry OS (proprietary conversational-interaction stack on Unitree G1 hardware)
price_note: Reservation price on Lightberry's own site for Founder Edition units shipping in 2026. Lumi is a branded interaction platform built on a customized Unitree G1 hardware base (29 DoF chassis extended to 34 DoF with added grippers), sold and supported by Lightberry rather than through Unitree's own store.

European retail launch pricing announced at IFA Berlin 2026: $1,000-$1,500 per unit through distributors newly signed in Germany and Belgium. An early Forbes preview in January 2026 had floated under $600 for a consumer version; the confirmed launch price is well above that estimate. First production run is only 100 units, with a separate B2B configuration (behavioral-tracking dashboard for care providers) priced separately and not disclosed.
